name: Mississippi

ttd.rateText: Two-thirds (2/3) of the claimant's average weekly wage at the time of injury, subject to a maximum calculated annually under Miss. Code Ann. § 71-3-13 (MWCC FAQ).
ttd.minText: No minimum weekly rate was found on the MWCC pages read.
ttd.periodLabel: injuries on or after January 1, 2026 (total disability payable up to a lifetime maximum of $294,583.50 = 450 weeks x $654.63)

waiting.text: Waiting-period rule not found on the MWCC pages that could be read; the statute (Miss. Code Ann. § 71-3-11) was not accessible.

ttdDuration.text: Wage-loss benefits are subject to statutory time limits; the MWCC rate table states a lifetime disability maximum equal to 450 times the weekly maximum ($294,583.50 for 2026 injuries).

ppd.text: Once the doctor finds maximum medical improvement, 'permanent disability' wage-loss payments may be due if the worker has a permanent disability or handicap, at up to two-thirds of the average weekly wage subject to the weekly maximum and statutory time limits (MWCC, Workers' Compensation Facts).

statute.cite: Miss. Code Ann. § 71-3-13 (maximum), Mississippi Workers' Compensation Law, Title 71, Chapter 3

facts.text: Employers with five or more regularly employed workers must carry workers' compensation; coverage is voluntary below five, and domestic and farm labor are excluded unless covered voluntarily (MWCC, Workers' Compensation Facts).

The injured worker may select one physician or provider of his or her choosing (a chiropractor is allowed), and that provider may make one referral to a specialist without carrier approval (MWCC, Workers' Compensation Facts).
If no disability benefits are paid, the claim is barred unless filed with the Commission within two years of the injury (MWCC, Workers' Compensation Facts).
Death benefits can continue for up to 450 weeks; the employer also pays up to $5,000 in funeral expenses and an immediate $1,000 lump sum to the surviving spouse (MWCC, Workers' Compensation Facts).
Medical mileage reimbursement is $0.725 per mile from January 1, 2026 (MWCC rate page).

uncertain: mwcc.ms.gov blocks automated access (Cloudflare 403). The rate table was read from the site's own page script (scripts/controllers/maximumBenefitMileageRatesChartController.js) via a Wayback Machine snapshot of 2026-06-04; the table there is a 'fallback' list in a CMS controller, so the live page may differ.

CONFLICT: a February 2025 snapshot of the same MWCC script listed 2023 $585.82, 2024 $608.58, 2025 $630.73, while the 2026 snapshot lists 2023 $570.00, 2024 $590.00, 2025 $610.00 and 2026 $654.63. The 2026 figure should be confirmed on the live MWCC page or a Commission bulletin before publishing.

Minimum weekly benefit, waiting period and PPD schedule (Miss. Code Ann. §§ 71-3-11, 71-3-13, 71-3-17) could not be read from an official source; the code is hosted by LexisNexis (linked by MWCC), which was not used.
